related_questions.question: What is the current protocol for a positive COVID test?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, the current recommendation is to isolate for at least five days from the start of symptoms or from the day of the positive test if asymptomatic, and to wear a mask for a total of 10 days. You can end isolation earlier if symptoms are gone or improving, and you've been fever-free for 24 hours without medication. Inform your close contacts and take precautions.
snippet_highlighted_words: isolate for at least five days from the start of symptoms or from the day of the positive test if asymptomatic, and to wear a mask for a total of 10 days

list.snippet: Isolate: Stay home and away from others to prevent further spread.
Seek medical care: Consult with a healthcare provider for appropriate treatment.
Masking: Wear a high-quality mask (like an N95 or KN95) when around others for 10 days, even after isolation ends.
Monitor symptoms: If symptoms worsen, seek medical attention.
Inform contacts: Notify close contacts of your positive test result so they can take appropriate precautions.
End isolation: You can end isolation after at least five days if symptoms are gone or improving and you've been fever-free for 24 hours without medication.

related_questions.question: What should I do if I test positive for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: If you test positive for COVID-19, immediately contact your healthcare provider to discuss your situation and potential treatment options, especially if you have underlying health conditions or severe symptoms. Rest, stay hydrated, and manage symptoms with over-the-counter medications as needed. Monitor your symptoms closely and report any worsening symptoms to your doctor. If you experience severe symptoms like difficulty breathing or chest pain, seek immediate emergency care by calling 911.
snippet_highlighted_words: immediately contact your healthcare provider to discuss your situation and potential treatment options

list.snippet: Inform your doctor about your positive test result.
They can assess your individual situation and provide tailored advice, including potential treatment options.
Rest: Allow your body to recover by getting plenty of sleep.
Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated.
Symptom Management: Over-the-counter medications can help alleviate symptoms like fever, headache, and muscle aches.
Keep track of your symptoms: Note any changes or worsening symptoms.
Communicate with your doctor: Report any concerning symptoms to your healthcare provider promptly.
Severe symptoms: If you experience difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain, confusion, or other emergency warning signs, call 911 immediately and inform them you have COVID-19.
